seasonal:eid-al-fitr.title: The festival after Ramadan (Eid al-Fitr)
keyPoints: Cites Sahih Muslim 1164: fasting Ramadan then six days of Shawwal is like fasting perpetually; says ask a teacher whether owed make-up fasts come first.
Says Eid day itself is not a day for fasting; no hadith on the ban on fasting the two Eids is among its sourceIds.
Says 'many Muslims give' Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid prayer, leaving amount and who pays to local scholars; never says it is obligatory on those able. Cites Abu Dawud 1609.
Says to eat something small before leaving for the prayer, since this is the Eid after the fasting (cites Bukhari 953).
Describes Eid prayer as short, held in a masjid, hall or park, usually followed by a khutbah or reminder (Bukhari 964, Muslim 886a, Abu Dawud 1149, SeekersGuidance).
Scripts ask work or school for the Eid morning off and tell non-Muslim family about the morning prayer; the 'on your own' section suggests messaging a mentor.
preCheckFlags: Naming rule: heading 'Zakat al-Fitr in brief' leads with the Arabic term instead of plain English.

seasonal:dhul-hijjah-hajj-umrah.title: Pilgrimage season (Hajj and Dhul Hijjah)
keyPoints: Says fasting the Day of Arafah is recommended for those not on Hajj who are able ('strongly encouraged in hadith'); cites Muslim 1162b.
Says Hajj is a pillar, obligatory once physically and financially able (no Quran 3:97 among sources), and that qurbani/udhiyah details vary by school, income and charity.
Defines Umrah as 'a pilgrimage to Makkah outside the Hajj season'; confirm the wording, since in fiqh Umrah is not limited to outside the Hajj months.
Says travel.gc.ca (checked Sept 2026) expects Hajj around 14-19 May 2027 and advised avoiding non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia, stricter in some regions.
Says Canada was on Nusuk Hajj's serviced list for 2026, the 2027 list was unpublished on 23 Sep 2026, registering is no guarantee, and Umrah can use any visa type.
Health: yellow fever proof only if arriving via a yellow fever country; no meningococcal rule stated (defers to Nusuk). Says a masjid conversion certificate may be needed.
preCheckFlags: Naming rule: headings 'Qurbani and udhiyah in brief', 'Hajj as something ahead of you', 'Umrah basics' and link label 'Zakat and Hajj step' lead with Arabic, not plain English.

seasonal:zakat.title: Yearly charity (zakat) for beginners
keyPoints: Nisab: Islamic Relief Canada 87.48 g gold or 612.36 g silver; NZF Canada 85 g or 595 g; Muslim Welfare Canada calculator 88 g or 613 g. Confirm each against the live pages.
Says 2.5 percent on cash and savings, or 2.577 percent on a calendar year; hawl is one lunar year (about 354 days) above nisab; gold vs silver nisab left to a scholar.
New Muslims: no zakat for years before Islam; first zakat a lunar year after Shahada (SeekersGuidance, Irshaad Sedick, 2022, Shafi'i); NZF: most scholars allow paying early.
Cites NZF (Sheikh Nabil Khan, 2022): Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali exempt worn women's jewellery, Hanafi requires zakat on all gold and silver; also NZF's RRSP/TFSA method.
Says most scholars limit zakat to Muslims (help non-Muslim family with sadaqah); Penny Appeal counts new converts among 'those whose hearts are to be reconciled' (Quran 9:60).
Charity numbers: IRC 821896875RR0001, MWC 89733-1732-RR0001, NZF 839912599RR0001, Penny Appeal 827502741 RR0001 (not CRA-checked); CRA tax credit on line 34900.
preCheckFlags: Naming rule: heading 'Nisab, hawl, and 2.5 percent' and link label 'Zakat and Hajj step' lead with Arabic terms instead of plain English.

seasonal:islamic-calendar.title: Islamic calendar guide for beginners
keyPoints: Says communities follow local sighting, a regional or global announcement, or a calculated calendar, and advises following the masjid you pray and celebrate with.
Says Muharram is the first month and holds Ashura, Shawwal opens with Eid al-Fitr, Dhul Hijjah holds Hajj and Eid al-Adha, and Rajab and Sha'ban precede Ramadan.
Cites Quran 2:189 and 9:36, Bukhari 1909 (moon sighting) and 4662 (sacred months); also cites the AlAdhan prayer-times API, not the FCNA calendar the site's dates use.

seasonal:muharram-ashura.title: The first month and Ashura (Muharram)
keyPoints: Says Muharram is one of the four sacred months named in hadith (Bukhari 4662; Quran 9:36) and Ashura is its tenth day.
Says voluntary fasting in Muharram and on Ashura is in authentic hadith (Muslim 1163a, Bukhari 2004) and ties Ashura to gratitude to Allah; not the Ramadan fast.
Suggests asking whether the community fasts one day or two; no hadith on adding the ninth day (e.g. Muslim 1134) is among its sourceIds.
'If the day feels heavy' alludes to communities marking painful history in Muharram without naming Karbala; confirm the wording is respectful and neutral.
Warns against unsourced Ashura rituals, promises and viral checklists; confirm this does not dismiss practices mainstream Sunni scholars accept.

seasonal:rabi-al-awwal-seerah.title: The Prophet's birth month (Rabi al-Awwal)
keyPoints: Title (and the seasonal calendar) calls Rabi al-Awwal the Prophet's birth month; sourceIds are general (Quran 21:107, 33:21, 68:4, seerah links), none specific to the birth month.
On Mawlid and commemorations: says Muslims differ and a beginner need not take a side; confirm this neutral framing fits mainstream Sunni positions.
Belief statements: the Prophet is the Messenger of Allah and the example believers follow; his message is worshipping Allah alone.
Suggests sending blessings on the Prophet 'using a wording you have actually been taught' and taking on one Sunnah of character this month.
Its sources point beginners to Yaqeen Institute seerah videos, SeekersGuidance and New Muslim Academy.

seasonal:rajab-shaban-preparation.title: The months before Ramadan (Rajab and Sha'ban)
keyPoints: Says Rajab is named among the sacred months in hadith (Bukhari 4662) and warns against presenting any specific Rajab prayer, fast or promise as established without a source.
Says authentic hadith report the Prophet fasting often in Sha'ban (Bukhari 1969); advises asking a teacher how voluntary fasts fit health and schedule.
Cautions about 'a special night' seen online without naming mid-Sha'ban or Isra and Mi'raj; confirm this reflects the range of Sunni views on the night of mid-Sha'ban.
Tells readers to ask early about medication, illness, travel, menstruation, missed fasts and fidyah before Ramadan.

seasonal:year-round-charity-service.title: Charity and service all year
keyPoints: Says zakat is obligatory once its conditions apply and sadaqah is voluntary; says service and everyday decency count as charity (cites Muslim 1005).
Cites Quran 2:261 and 9:60; also lists LaunchGood's zakat policy and Islamic Relief Canada's nisab page as sources.
Advises giving only what you can afford, not cutting into rent, food or dependants, and walking away from pressure, vague emergency claims and anonymous payment links.
Lists 'announcing your donations publicly' under what can wait; says the page does not calculate zakat or advise on tax, investments or fundraising law.

resource:clear-quran-translation.title: The Clear Quran by Dr. Mustafa Khattab
keyPoints: Recommends The Clear Quran, Dr. Mustafa Khattab's plain-English translation of the meaning (theclearquran.org), for first-time readers.
trustNote says to use translations as meanings, not as a replacement for the Arabic Quran.

resource:welcome-to-islam-book.title: Welcome to Islam: A Step-by-Step Guide for New Muslims
keyPoints: Recommends Mustafa Umar's 'Welcome to Islam: A Step-by-Step Guide for New Muslims' for the first month after Shahada.
trustNote says it is 32 pages and free to read online; confirm (sources.json: CreateSpace 2011, ISBN 9781461104773).
trustNote says the author is an imam and a member of the Fiqh Council of North America; confirm current membership.

resource:quran-com.title: Quran.com
keyPoints: Recommends Quran.com (Quran.Foundation) for reading, translations, transliteration and audio recitation.
trustNote says it is a nonprofit with no ads, needs no account, and uses Google Analytics; confirm against the current privacy policy.
bestFor says 'comparing translations'; confirm the English translations it offers are ones the team is comfortable pointing beginners to.

resource:new-muslim-academy.title: New Muslim Academy
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Academy (newmuslimacademy.org) for structured beginner courses; the entry does not say who runs it. Confirm the operator and that its teachers are mainstream Sunni.
trustNote: 'Good for foundations. Take personal rulings to a qualified teacher.'

resource:yaqeen-institute.title: Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research
keyPoints: Recommends Yaqeen Institute (US-based, founded by Dr. Omar Suleiman) for faith questions and doubts; confirm it suits beginners.
Description says its articles and videos use 'sourced research'; trustNote says it gives context 'without turning early Islam into debate overload'.

resource:bayyinah-tv.title: Bayyinah TV
keyPoints: Recommends Bayyinah TV (Bayyinah, founded by Nouman Ali Khan per sources.json) for Quran and Arabic courses 'from the alphabet'; confirm suitability and the beginner courses.
trustNote gives $11 a month (checked 23 Sep 2026) and a free one-year hardship membership; confirm the price and whether it is USD or CAD.

resource:new-muslim-guide-icna.title: ICNA New Muslim Support
keyPoints: Recommends ICNA (Islamic Circle of North America) for new Muslim support, listing Embrace, WhyIslam and a converts' gathering.
trustNote says its pages focus on the United States and to ask a local masjid for Canada; confirm whether ICNA Canada has new Muslim programs to link instead.

resource:whyislam.title: WhyIslam
keyPoints: Recommends WhyIslam for introductions, one-on-one conversations and new Muslim support; the entry names 'WhyIslam' as the organisation, sources.json names ICNA.
bestFor suggests it for explaining Islam to family members; confirm its hotline and programs serve people in Canada.

resource:learn-salah-guide.title: New Muslim Guide - Prayer
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Guide's prayer section (newmuslimguide.com) for preparing, prayer times and what to learn first; the publisher is not named in the entry.
trustNote says scholars differ on some details; confirm the guide does not present one school's way of praying as the only valid one.

resource:new-muslim-guide-site.title: New Muslim Guide
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Guide (newmuslimguide.com) as a 'one-stop beginner reference'; publisher not named (believed to be Dr. Fahd Salem Bahammam, Saudi Arabia): confirm.
trustNote: 'Best used for foundations, not as a personalized fatwa source.' Confirm its rulings acknowledge differences between the Sunni schools.

resource:quran-recitation-mishary.title: Quran Recitation by Mishary Rashid Alafasy
keyPoints: Recommends Mishary Rashid Alafasy's recitation via quran.com/reciters/7; confirm the link opens his recitation.
trustNote: listen slowly and learn to recite with a teacher.

resource:ramadan-guide-yaqeen.title: Ramadan Resources by Yaqeen Institute
keyPoints: Recommends Yaqeen Institute's Ramadan page (yaqeeninstitute.org/ramadan) for spiritual preparation and practical reminders.
trustNote says personal fasting exceptions should be reviewed with a qualified local scholar.

resource:khalil-center.title: Khalil Center - Muslim Mental Health
keyPoints: Recommends Khalil Center (khalilcenter.ca) for faith-sensitive therapy; sources.json says online only, phone 416-901-2244, some insurance accepted.
Confirm its clinicians are registered with Canadian provincial regulators (sources.json says the home page does not list registrations).
trustNote says it is not emergency care and to 'use crisis services' for immediate danger, naming neither 911 nor 9-8-8 (only the footer does).

resource:becoming-muslim-report.title: Becoming Muslim: The Lives of American Converts to Islam
keyPoints: Describes Yaqeen's 2025 report 'Becoming Muslim' (Umarji, Birawi, Desouky, Oduro) as a survey of 618 US converts; confirm year and sample size.
trustNote says it is about American converts and not a mental health guide, yet resource-collections lists it under 'Mental health and support'.

resource:seekers-guidance.title: SeekersGuidance
keyPoints: Recommends SeekersGuidance (founded by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani; Canada-based, confirm) for free courses and Q&A 'taught by qualified scholars'.
trustNote: 'Good for structured knowledge. Ask locally about your own circumstances.'

resource:being-muslim-book.title: Being Muslim: A Practical Guide
keyPoints: Recommends 'Being Muslim: A Practical Guide' from Sandala (Hamza Yusuf's publishing arm per sources.json); author not named in the entry (believed Asad Tarsin): confirm.
Description says it is for new and returning Muslims and covers worship, spirituality and community life.

resource:halal-living-guide.title: New Muslim Guide - Food and Drink
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Guide's food and drink section; description says it covers reading ingredients, eating out and 'knowing when you have checked enough': confirm.
trustNote says ingredient and certification details vary by country; confirm its halal rulings (e.g. on meat) fit Canadian practice across the Sunni schools.

resource:seerah-podcast.title: Seerah Series by Yasir Qadhi
keyPoints: Recommends Dr. Yasir Qadhi's Seerah lecture series (YouTube playlist PLAEA99D24CA2F9A8F); confirm the playlist and that the teacher suits new Muslims.
trustNote says it goes deeper than a first-week resource; sources.json says the episode count was not checked.

resource:wudu-tutorial.title: New Muslim Guide - Purification
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Guide's purification section for wudu, ghusl and ritual purity; confirm its rulings acknowledge differences between the Sunni schools.
Same title and URL as resource purification-fiqh-guide (newmuslimguide.com/en/categories/your-purification); confirm both entries are needed.

resource:convert-story-videos.title: Convert Stories - The Deen Show

trustNote: stories are personal experiences, not sources for rulings.

resource:aboutislam-new-muslims.title: AboutIslam - New Muslims
keyPoints: Recommends AboutIslam's New Muslims section (aboutislam.net) for short articles on faith, identity, family and community; publisher not named: confirm who runs it.

resource:purification-fiqh-guide.title: New Muslim Guide - Purification

resource:naseeha-mental-health.title: Naseeha helpline

LaunchGood is a crowdfunding platform (not a CRA-registered charity, confirm); check what readers should know about Canadian tax receipts before giving there.

resource:yaqeen-dhul-hijjah-resources.title: Yaqeen Institute - Dhul Hijjah Resources
keyPoints: Recommends Yaqeen Institute's Dhul Hijjah playlist; description says it has simple worship ideas for the first ten days: confirm the series matches.

Description says it covers handling the mushaf, reading translations and etiquette 'so you do not panic'; trustNote sends detailed purity questions to a local teacher.

collection:resource-collections.title: Resource collections, feature cards, choosing checklist and warnings
keyPoints: 'Mental health and support' is described as 'Counselors and crisis lines that understand faith' and lists Khalil Center, Naseeha and a Yaqeen report; 911 and 9-8-8 appear only in the site footer.
'Mentor resources' points mentors to ICNA and WhyIslam (US-focused), New Muslim Academy and SeekersGuidance's Essentials course; confirm the Canadian fit.
'Zakat and giving' says it is enough to understand how zakat works but lists only the CRA charity list, the CAFC fraud page and SeekersGuidance.
Checklist and warnings: check who made a resource, skip anonymous fatwa screenshots and debate channels, and walk away from teaching that pressures, isolates or shames.
preCheckFlags: 'Mental health and support' body says 'Counselors and crisis lines' but lists becoming-muslim-report, whose own trustNote says it is 'not a mental health guide'.
Naming rule: collection heading 'Zakat and giving' leads with Arabic (the site's own title is 'Yearly charity (zakat) for beginners').

collection:seasonal-calendar.title: Seasonal calendar dates (Coming up pointer)
keyPoints: Note: approximate dates from the FCNA calculated calendar; local sighting may differ by a day or two. 14 seasons, 14 Aug 2026 to 15 Jan 2029 (1448-1450 AH); the first is past.
1448: Rabi al-Awwal 14 Aug-12 Sep 2026; Rajab-Sha'ban 10 Dec 2026-7 Feb 2027; Ramadan 8 Feb-8 Mar 2027; Eid al-Fitr 9-11 Mar; Dhul Hijjah 7-19 May 2027.
1449: Muharram 6 Jun-4 Jul 2027; Rabi al-Awwal 3 Aug-1 Sep; Rajab-Sha'ban 29 Nov-27 Jan 2028; Ramadan 28 Jan-25 Feb 2028; Eid 26-28 Feb; Dhul Hijjah 26 Apr-8 May.
1450: Muharram 25 May-22 Jun 2028; Rabi al-Awwal 23 Jul-21 Aug; Rajab-Sha'ban to 15 Jan 2029. Our new-moon check puts 3 ends a day off: 11 Sep 2026, 23 Jun and 20 Aug 2028.
